name: L-165041
lead: L-165041 is a research chemical that selectively activates PPAR-delta (PPARbeta/delta), a nuclear receptor involved in the regulation of fatty acid metabolism. It is used in laboratory studies of lipid metabolism, heart, blood vessel and nerve cell biology, and is listed by chemical suppliers as a research tool.[2][3]

Published work consists of cell-culture and animal experiments. In insulin-resistant db/db mice, treatment with L-165041 altered lipid metabolism,[2] and in cultured rat heart cells it reduced hypertrophic responses.[3] No published human study has tested it for fat loss or any appearance-related purpose.
It appears in fat-loss discussions as a compound in the same pathway as better-known PPAR-delta agonists studied as exercise mimetics.

paras: L-165041 binds and activates PPAR-delta, which partners with the retinoid X receptor to regulate gene expression.[2] In cardiac cells, PPARbeta/delta activation modulates genes of fatty acid handling.[1] Reporter-cell assays have compared its selectivity with other synthetic PPAR ligands.[6]

In db/db mice, a PPAR-delta agonist including L-165041 changed lipid metabolism parameters.[2] In cultured neonatal rat cardiomyocytes it inhibited phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy.[3] Other lab studies report anti-inflammatory effects in endothelial cells,[4] neuroprotective effects in models,[5] endothelial survival effects,[7] and protection in a kidney injury model.[8] These are animal and cell findings and do not establish effects in people.
No studies found. Research on the compound is limited to cell and animal experiments.

The compound is sold as a research chemical and is not approved as a medicine. A general PPAR-delta agonist concept as an exercise mimetic was described in a 2008 Cell paper using a different PPAR-delta agonist.[9]

timeline.event: Mouse study reports PPAR-delta activation by L-165041 alters lipid metabolism in db/db mice.[2]
Study reports inhibition of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy.[3]

card.note: Research chemical with no human studies.

quick.overview:
L-165041 is a laboratory compound that switches on PPAR-delta, a receptor that helps control how cells handle fats.

It has been used in cell and rodent experiments on metabolism, heart, vessel and nerve biology. It has not been tested in people for fat loss.
quick.mechanism: It binds PPAR-delta, which regulates genes involved in fatty acid metabolism.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. It is a research chemical and not an approved medicine.
